hubIntro.documents: The Documents category covers everyday writing and text tasks. Count the words in an essay or article, clean up text pasted from a PDF or Word file, change capitalization for variable names or titles, compare two drafts, or remove duplicate entries from a list. Your browser processes the text and nothing goes to a server, so you can use these tools on private or sensitive writing.
hubIntro.pdf: The PDF category handles everyday document jobs. Merge several files into one, split a long document into parts, shrink a file for email, rotate pages that came out upside down from a scan, pull out specific pages, or extract text. Your browser processes each file, so contracts and ID scans stay on your device.
hubIntro.spreadsheet: The Spreadsheet category handles everyday tabular data. View a CSV file without opening Excel, clean messy data, split a large file into parts, merge several files into one, or convert between CSV and Excel. Your browser processes each file and nothing reaches a server, so internal and sensitive data stays private.
hubIntro.data: The Data category holds conversion and cleanup tools for developers and analysts. Turn a JSON API response into a CSV table you can open in Excel, convert spreadsheet data into JSON for your code, work with legacy XML, or tidy and validate a data structure before you use it. The conversion runs in your browser, so sensitive and internal data stays with you.
hubIntro.productivity: The Productivity category has calculators for everyday operational work. Work out discounts and business margins, project a deadline in business days, find the exact difference between two dates, total working hours across several shifts, or add up time durations. Each calculation runs in your browser, so you don't need a separate spreadsheet app.

faq.question: Can nested JSON be converted?
faq.answer: Yes. The tool flattens nested objects into columns with combined names. {'{'} "address": {'{'} "city": "Bandung" {'}'} {'}'} becomes the column address.city. CSV has no concept of nesting, so flattening keeps your data intact.

faq.question: What happens when array items have different fields?
faq.answer: The tool combines every column found across your data into one header. Objects missing a field get an empty cell there.

faq.question: Does my JSON have to be an array?
faq.answer: No. A single object works too. The tool wraps it into one row automatically.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. The conversion runs in your browser from start to finish.

faq.question: Does the first row need to hold column names?
faq.answer: Yes. The first CSV row becomes the header and supplies the keys in the JSON output.

faq.question: What about a comma inside a cell?
faq.answer: Wrap that cell in double quotes, like "text, with a comma". This is standard CSV format and the tool supports it.

faq.question: Are data types like numbers detected automatically?
faq.answer: No. Every value becomes text in the JSON output, since CSV itself carries no type information.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded to a server?

xml-to-csv.howToTitle: How to convert XML to CSV
steps: Paste your XML in the left column.
Watch the CSV result appear in the right column.
Click Copy to copy it, or Download to save it as a .csv file.
useCase: A legacy system or API still sends data as XML, but you need to analyze it in Excel or Google Sheets.

faq.question: What XML structure can this tool convert?
faq.answer: XML with repeating elements that share a tag name as children of one root, for example several <item> tags inside <items>. Each repeating element becomes one table row.

faq.question: What if my XML has no repeating elements?
faq.answer: The tool treats the whole document as a single row. Each child tag becomes one column.

faq.question: Are XML attributes converted too?
faq.answer: Not yet. The tool reads only the text inside tags. Attributes on a tag, like id="1", aren't supported yet.

faq.question: Is my data uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. The conversion runs in your browser from start to finish.

faq.question: What's the difference between Format and Minify?
faq.answer: Format adds indentation so people can read it easily. Minify strips every space and line break to shrink the file, suited for production.

faq.question: Is minify available for XML too?

word-counter.howToTitle: How to count words and characters
steps: Paste or type your text into the box.
Watch the word, character, sentence, and paragraph counts appear automatically.
Use the Copy button to copy the summary.
Click Clear to empty the text and start a new count.
useCase: Essays and assignments often carry a minimum or maximum word count. Paste your draft here and see the result right away, no manual counting.

faq.question: Does a space count as a character?
faq.answer: Yes. We show two separate numbers: characters with spaces and without, so you can match whatever a platform or institution asks for.

faq.question: How are paragraphs counted?
faq.answer: A paragraph is a block of text separated by a blank line (two line breaks). Keep your paragraph formatting consistent for an accurate count.

faq.question: Is there a limit on how much text I can count?
faq.answer: No official limit. Everything runs in your browser, so the real limit depends on your device.

faq.question: Is the text I enter stored on a server?
faq.answer: No. Word Counter runs entirely in your browser. Your text is never sent, uploaded, or stored anywhere.

faq.question: Does this match Word Count in Microsoft Word?
faq.answer: Usually. Small differences can show up depending on how each app counts punctuation or empty paragraphs.

faq.question: Which formats are supported?
faq.answer: Eight formats: UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Sentence case, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and kebab-case. Useful for writing and for naming variables in code.

faq.question: Can camelCase and PascalCase work on regular text?
faq.answer: Yes, though both work best on short phrases without punctuation. Both strip spaces between words, matching how programming variable names get built.

faq.question: Does Sentence case fix random capitals mid-sentence?
faq.answer: Yes. Sentence case lowercases everything first, then capitalizes the first letter of each sentence and the letter after a period, question mark, or exclamation point.

faq.question: Is my text stored on a server?

faq.question: Does this compare word by word or line by line?

faq.question: What do the red and green colors mean?
faq.answer: A red line on the left only exists in the first text (removed). A green line on the right only exists in the second text (added).

faq.question: Can it compare very long documents?
faq.answer: Yes. Since the comparison runs in your browser, documents with thousands of lines can slow down a lower-spec device.

faq.question: Are both texts uploaded to a server?

faq.question: Does the line order stay the same?
faq.answer: Yes. The first occurrence of each line keeps its position. Later repeats get removed.

faq.question: What's the difference between case-sensitive and not?
faq.answer: With case-sensitive on, "Apple" and "apple" count as two different lines. Turn it off and both count as the same, with one removed as a duplicate.

faq.question: Does leading/trailing whitespace affect duplicate detection?
faq.answer: With Trim whitespace per line on, leading and trailing spaces get ignored during comparison. "word " and "word" then count as the same.
